messages:
Ashley: Heads-up — Acme asked for WORM-backed audit exports with customer-owned KMS keys and proof-of-retention (7y). They want verifiable chain-of-custody. What scope do we have?
Miguel: Are they after S3 Object Lock (COMPLIANCE) or just signed, time-stamped bundles? Need to clarify legal hold semantics.
amanda_legal: @Ashley please loop legal. For regulated customers we need a manifest + signatures and a clear retention/hold policy.
Samir: Quick note: current export job writes JSONL to our shared bucket. We don't set Object Lock or embed HMACs today. Backfills exist.
Jen: If we enable Object Lock we should provision dedicated buckets per customer (or per account), and require a CMK with a do-not-delete policy. Rotation semantics for CMKs matter.
sre-bot: deploy/export-job v1.14 completed — export pipeline doesn't yet generate signed manifests.
Ashley: So proposed deliverables: 1) schema additions for signature/retention metadata, 2) export pipeline change to produce sealed manifests + per-file hashes, 3) bucket provisioning with Object Lock + CMK, 4) RBAC changes so only admins can enable WORM. Thoughts on the schema?
Miguel: Draft schema snippet: 
```json
{
  "event_id": "uuid",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-20T15:12:00Z",
  "actor": {"id":"user:123","type":"user"},
  "action": "auth.login",
  "resource": "api:token",
  "signature": {
    "sig": "base64(...)",
    "algo": "ed25519",
    "key_id": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-1234"
  },
  "storage": {
    "bucket": "acme-audit-2026",
    "object_lock": "COMPLIANCE",
    "retention_until": "2033-03-20T00:00:00Z"
  }
}
```
Ashley: Nice. How do we let customers validate signatures + immutability proofs? They want to be able to independently verify.
Samir: Two pieces: produce a signed manifest per export (manifest lists file names + SHA256 per file + merkle root) and sign the manifest with our platform signing key. Put the merkle root in object metadata too. For customer-owned CMKs we can include an attestation that lists the CMK ARN used to encrypt the object.
Jen: From RBAC side: new permission 'exports.worm.configure' scoped to org-admin + security-admin. Console needs an explicit opt-in flow and a warning about irreversible deletes. Audit trail must record who enabled and timestamp.
amanda_legal: Confirming: we need attestation language that states "these exports were sealed on DATE using CMK <ARN> and stored under Object Lock compliance mode". Also request we provide a verification CLI or small script.
Ashley: Edge-case: if customer rotates/deletes CMK, they could lose ability to decrypt. We need guidance: either require a deny-delete key policy or offer an escrow/backup key option.
Miguel: Recommend offering two modes: customer-managed CMK (recommended) or Redwood-escrowed CMK (for recovery). Document cryptographic guarantees for each.
Samir: Implementation notes: write/export pipeline should write to staging bucket, compute SHA256s, build manifest, sign manifest, then copy objects to WORM bucket in a single atomic step (move or copy+verify) to avoid partial sets. Backfill process must be able to 'seal' historical exports.
Jen: Tasks: infra PR for bucket + KMS provisioning automation, export service update to attach signatures and metadata, console opt-in + RBAC change, legal attestation text, e2e verification tests. Rough ETA: 3 sprints if we prioritize.
Ashley: I'll draft the spec and attach compliance checklist. @Jen @Miguel can you own infra + pipeline pairing? I'll loop legal after draft. :thumbsup:
